headline: Recommended acceptance of grants and donations, a $12,000 wayfinding sign transfer, and a fee-notice ordinance change; withdrew Recovery Coach Academy request.
summary: The committee recommended City Council acceptance of several donations and state grants, including a $95,636.25 911 training grant and a $102,983 911 support grant. It also recommended two police detail budget transfers, a $12,000 transfer for the Wayfinding Signs Project, and an ordinance change removing a newspaper-publication requirement for fee changes. A request to use funds for the Recovery Coach Academy was withdrawn, and the Auditor's report on deficit accounts drew no motion.

Recommended that the City Council accept $2,785.00 in donations for Veterans Services, roll call 3-0.

Recommended that the City Council accept the FY2027 State 911 Training Grant of $95,636.25, roll call 3-0.
Recommended that the City Council accept the FY27 State 911 Support and Incentive Grant of $102,983, roll call 3-0.
Recommended City Council approval of Special Budgetary Transfer #2027-SBT-1 for $9,922.24 for police details, roll call 3-0.
Recommended City Council approval of Special Budgetary Transfer #2027-SBT-2 for $401.33 for police details, roll call 3-0.
Recommended City Council approval of Supplemental Appropriation #2027-SA-3 of $12,000 to install part of the Wayfinding Signs project, roll call 3-0.
Recommended that the City Council amend Chapter 2, Article 2, Section 28 'Fees' to delete the newspaper publication requirement, roll call 3-0.

Budget & Finance Standing Committee

-Minutes-
Present: Chair Councilor Scott Memhard; Vice Chair Councilor Tony Gross; Councilor Patti-Ann
Page (remote)
Also Present: CAO, Kelly Dolan; City Clerk, Grace Poirier; Auditor, Kenny Costa (remote);
Acting Police Chief, Michael Gossom
Meeting called to order at 5:30 p.m.
This meeting was conducted in-person and remotely via ZOOM.
Councilor Memhard announced the names of the B&F Committee members in attendance and City staff
who were in attendance in person and on Zoom.
1. Memorandum from the Archives Committee requesting acceptance of donations in the amount

Gross, the Budget & Finance Committee voted by ROLL CALL, 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to recommend
that the City Council approve Special Budgetary Transfer #2027-SBT-2 in the amount of $401.33 from
General Fund, Registration, Ordinary Maintenance - Police Details, Account #0116352-530018, to
General Fund, Police – Uniform, Personal Services - Shift Differentials, Account #0121151-514004, for
the reimbursement for police details for the September 1, 2026 State Primary. 
8. Memorandum from the City Auditor & #2027-SA-3 in the amount of $12,000 to install a portion
of the Wayfinding Signs Project
Summary of Discussion: Auditor, Kenny Costa stated that these funds had been part of the end-of year
transfers in FY26, and this was moving the funds back from the General Fund to the Tourism budget. 
CAO, Kelly Dolan stated that all the signs had been installed.
Councilor Page stated that the total amount for the Wayfinding Signs Project was $181,410 and asked
for clarification what this portion would be used for. Kenny Costa stated that the actual amount was
$169,410. He stated that the portion had been transferred and retained for reporting purposes. 
Councilor Page stated that the placement of the sign on the boulevard was poorly chosen.
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Memhard, seconded by Councilor
Gross, the Budget & Finance Committee voted by ROLL CALL, 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to recommend
Budget & Finance                               October 8, 2026                                     Page 4 of 5
that the City Council approve Supplemental Appropriation #2027-SA-3 in the amount of $12,000
(Twelve Thousand Dollars) from the General Stabilization Fund – Undesignated Fund Balance Account
#7500-359000 to the General Fund, Tourism – Other Purchase of Services #0156352-538000. The
purpose of this appropriation is to install a portion of the Wayfinding Signs project.
9. CC#2026-018 (Gross): Amend Ch. 2 “Administration,” Art. 2 “City Council,” Sec. 28 “Fees”
by DELETING “and published in a local newspaper whenever fee changes or new fees are
approved by the City Council.”
Summary of Discussion: City Clerk, Grace Poirier stated that this ordinance amendment was meant
to bring the ordinance in line with current practice. She stated that the ordinance currently states when a
fee is updated it needed to be published on the City website as well as the local newspaper. She stated
that for many years fee changes had not been published in the newspaper. She stated the City was in the
process of getting all fees posted on the website, and the proposed ordinance amendment would remove
the requirement of publishing it in the newspaper. 
Councilor Gross stated that previous City Councils had voted to move all fees from the ordinance to fee
schedules, but that had not yet occurred. He stated that this was for fees that had been approved and not
just proposed. 
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Memhard, seconded by Councilor
Gross, the Budget & Finance Committee voted by ROLL CALL, 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to recommend
that the City Council amend Gloucester Code of Ordinances Chapter 2 “Administration,” Art. 2 “City
Council,” Sec. 28 “Fees” as follows:
“All fees contained in the city schedule of fees are hereby established and authorized. Said fees may be
modified from time to time by vote of the city council unless the fees are governed and controlled by
M.G.L. The schedule shall be posted on the city website [DELETE] and published in a local newspaper
whenever fee changes or new fees are approved by the city council.”
10. Memorandum from the City Auditor regarding accounts having expenditures which exceed
their authorization & Auditor’s Report and other related business
Summary of Discussion: Kenny Costa stated that there were fifteen accounts in deficit and there was
an overall decrease in the total amount since last report. He stated that several departments had fixed
their deficits, and he was currently working with the Harbormaster’s to resolve an issue with how payroll
was being split between the Harbormaster and the Shellfish Department.
Councilor Page stated that the cost of the Wayfinding Sign Project was too high.
No motion offered.
MOTION: On a motion by Councilor Gross, seconded by Councilor Memhard, the Budget &
Finance Committee voted by ROLL CALL, 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to adjourn at 6:00 p.m.
Submitted by: Lynds Jones, Legislative Aide.
Documents submitted at the meeting: None.
